clue.text: Game when precise hiss can be tricky?

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and twisty, so the three words before it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A party game where a phrase like 'precise hiss' gets hard to pass on accurately.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the game is exactly one where whispered words get garbled, as 'can be tricky' does to WHEN PRECISE HISS.
explanation.definitionFit: A party game in which a message passed along a line in murmurs ends up distorted.

clue.text: European bird from a large land mass making itself heard

indicators.note: something heard is spoken out, so the phrase before is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.words: bird from a large land mass
parts.note: a crow is a bird, and one from the largest continent is Asian: crow Asian

explanation.surface: A bird from a big continent calls out loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' looks like an adjective for the bird, but it is the definition: a person from Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country in Europe, so a native of it is a European.

clue.text: Sneer makes you stop short, last thing Pasquale wants

parts.note: to jib is to stop short and refuse, as a horse does at a fence

indicators.note: the last thing of a word is its final letter, here taken from the setter's name

explanation.surface: The setter Pasquale grumbling that he does not want a sneer to halt you.
explanation.walkthrough: Pasquale is the setter's pseudonym; its final letter is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a taunting, mocking remark aimed at someone.

clue.text: Wally has to take food that's hard dunked in drink

indicators.note: something dunked is plunged into a liquid, so the letter for hard goes inside the drink

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey
to eat is to take food
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fool dunks his hard biscuit in his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wally' is British slang for a silly, foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal insults for a dim, stupid person.

clue.text: Money handler certain to go into the city (as of old)

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it, so the word for certain sits within the city

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A banker sure of going into the City of London, in old times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The city' tempts as London's financial district, but it is ancient UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging excessive interest is someone who deals in cash loans.

clue.text: West Indian tries to deceive mother and blokes

parts.note: mama is an informal word for mother
guys are blokes, men

explanation.surface: A Caribbean person tries to trick a mother and some men.
explanation.walkthrough: MAMAGUY is a Trinidadian verb meaning to fool or flatter someone deceptively.
explanation.definitionFit: In Caribbean English this verb means to tease, hoodwink or mislead with flattery.

clue.text: Decisive blow with a bit of a strike for money

parts.note: KO is a knockout, the boxing blow that ends a fight
a peck is a small, light strike, as by a bird's beak

explanation.surface: A knockout punch delivered alongside a little hit, for a cash prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian coin worth one hundredth of a rouble is a unit of currency.

clue.text: Plant screens lie in various positions, concealing antelope

indicators.note: concealing means holding something hidden inside, so the antelope sits within the scrambled letters
letters placed in various positions are rearranged

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A plant screens a lie by moving about, hiding an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screens' reads as a verb in the surface but is anagram fodder; 'in various positions' scrambles it with 'lie' into LESSERCINE, which 'concealing' then wraps around the antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow-flowered spring wildflower of the buttercup family is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Strength of princess sadly no longer in control

indicators.note: in places the princess inside the word for control

parts.note: to harness something is to control it, and a harness is a means of control
Princess Diana, known as Di, who sadly died

explanation.surface: A princess's resilience, sadly, no longer keeps her in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly no longer' tempts as an anagram signal, but it points to the late Princess Diana, Di.
explanation.definitionFit: Toughness and robustness are both forms of strength or endurance.

clue.text: Make up for lunch now?

definitions.meaning: to make amends for a wrong
lunchtime, ... o'clock, as a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether lunch might compensate for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong is to redress it; lunch is often eaten at one o'clock.

clue.text: Most miserly member in hiding place

indicators.note: in puts the member inside the hiding place

parts.note: a nest is a snug hiding place or retreat
an ear is a member, a part of the body

explanation.surface: The stingiest person keeps a body part in a secret hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAR is an old word for stingy, so its superlative means most miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean mean or tight-fisted, so its superlative describes the stingiest.

clue.text: They can't stop this person being overwhelmed by loud noises

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another is engulfed by it, so the setter sits inside the loud noises

parts.note: roars are loud noises
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: People who cannot halt, with the speaker drowned out by loud noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderers keep moving about and never settle in one place.

clue.text: Habit of admirer putting soldiers off

indicators.note: putting something off removes it, so the soldiers are dropped from the admirer

parts.note: a suitor is an admirer who courts someone
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An admirer's custom of putting soldiers off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like custom, but here it is clothing, as in a riding habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a set of clothes, like a nun's or rider's outfit.

clue.text: Material obtained by dog not dry inside — one using straw?

indicators.note: not removes the letters for dry from inside the dog

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol, i.e. dry
someone drinking through a straw sucks, so is a sucker

explanation.surface: A fabric got hold of by a dog, with someone sipping through a straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not dry inside' says the teetotal letters come out from the middle of the dog's breed name; TT for teetotal is a crossword staple for 'dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin puckered cotton fabric, often striped, is a type of cloth.

clue.text: Bat was first to get dug out

parts.note: to bat an eyelid is to wink or blink
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A bat was the first creature to be dug out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' looks like the animal, but it is the verb for flicking an eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something with effort, as winkles are prised from shells, is to dig it out.

clue.text: See Urquhart Castle here and see church on headland

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A tourist directive to view a Scottish castle and a church on a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Urquhart Castle is a ruined castle in the Scottish Highlands standing on the shore of this famous loch.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruin of Urquhart Castle overlooks this Scottish lake, home of the legendary monster.

clue.text: Fail to notice this writer's communication

parts.note: to miss something is to fail to notice it
this writer's is the setter's 'I have', contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Overlooking the setter's message.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'writer's' is read as 'has', giving I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter or written message is a form of communication.

clue.text: No good going between two little women in system requiring one only!

indicators.note: going between means slotting into the gap between the two names

parts.note: Mo and Amy are short girls' names, Amy being one of the March sisters in Little Women
Amy, the youngest March sister in the novel Little Women
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something not good comes between two girls in a one-partner arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going between' slots NOG into the gap separating the two short names; the exclamation mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage to a single spouse is the arrangement that requires exactly one partner.

clue.text: Like form of calculus working out triangle

indicators.note: working something out reworks it, so the letters of triangle are rearranged

explanation.surface: Solving a triangle problem like a calculus exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Integration is one of the two main branches of calculus, so the adjective describes that branch.

clue.text: Charge cent — mind, it gets worse

indicators.note: something that gets worse is degraded into a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fee of a cent, but watch out, it increases.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal accusation of a crime is a legal charge.

clue.text: Scientist given challenge, shortly meeting with success

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the challenge is dropped

parts.note: a dare is a challenge
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A researcher faces a challenge and soon achieves success.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the English naturalist who proposed evolution by natural selection.

clue.text: Rock that upsets first half of country walk?

indicators.note: upsets means turns over, and it applies only to the opening half of the walk

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk in the countryside

explanation.surface: A boulder that disrupts the start of a countryside stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets first half of' turns RAM into MAR, leaving BLE in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A crystalline metamorphic limestone used in sculpture is a kind of stone.

clue.text: Sweet nature masks this one liable to erupt

indicators.note: masks means conceals within, so the answer is tucked inside the words sweet nature

explanation.surface: A gentle disposition covers up someone with a volcanic temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily's famous active volcano is a mountain prone to eruption.

clue.text: Colleague's role facing loveless persecutor

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

indicators.note: love is O in tennis scoring, so loveless removes an O from the persecutor

parts.note: the Roman emperor Nero persecuted Christians

explanation.surface: A co-worker's part is to face a cruel, unloving tormentor.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate one works alongside is a colleague.

clue.text: Tribe full of anger in building by house?

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the anger goes inside the tribe

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A tribe seething with fury in a structure beside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a car kept in the outbuilding beside a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A car put away in its shelter next to a home has been stored there.

clue.text: Game using stone

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
by can mean using, as in travel by car

explanation.surface: A game played using a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A red precious gem is a stone.

clue.text: Controls only half restored

indicators.note: only half keeps just the first half of the word for restored

parts.note: reinstated means restored to a former position

explanation.surface: Settings that have only been half put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' takes the first five of the ten letters of REINSTATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps used to guide a horse, and figuratively any means of control.

clue.text: Innocent person swallowing drug — wet person being stupid

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the drug goes inside the innocent person

parts.note: a lamb is an innocent, gentle person
E is ecstasy, a drug
rain is wet weather, or to rain is to be wet

explanation.surface: A naive person takes drugs, and a feeble fool acts dimly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like part of 'wet person', the British word for a weakling, but only gives RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit or idiot is someone being stupid.
